cells.question: What was gross revenue in January 2025 from our euro and yen orders, in US dollars?
cells.sql:
SELECT 
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN o.currency = 'EUR' THEN o.amount_minor * 1.10 / 100
            WHEN o.currency = 'JPY' THEN o.amount_minor * 0.0067 / 100
            ELSE 0
        END
    ) as gross_revenue_usd
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.currency IN ('EUR', 'JPY')
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.placed_at) = 2025
    AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.placed_at) = 1
    AND o.status != 'cancelled'
    AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND c.deleted_at IS NULL;

cells.question: What was gross revenue in January 2025 from our euro and yen orders, in US dollars?
cells.sql:
SELECT
  SUM(o.amount_minor * CASE o.currency
    WHEN 'EUR' THEN 0.0108
    WHEN 'JPY' THEN 0.0067
    WHEN 'USD' THEN 0.01
  END) AS gross_revenue_usd
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND o.status != 'cancelled'
  AND c.is_internal = FALSE
  AND o.currency IN ('EUR', 'JPY')
  AND DATE_TRUNC('month', o.placed_at) = '2025-01-01'::TIMESTAMP;

cells.question: What was net revenue in January 2025 from our euro and yen orders, in US dollars?
cells.sql:
SELECT 
  SUM(
    CASE 
      WHEN o.currency = 'EUR' THEN (o.amount_minor - COALESCE(SUM(r.amount_minor) OVER (PARTITION BY o.order_id), 0)) / 100.0 * 1.10
      WHEN o.currency = 'JPY' THEN (o.amount_minor - COALESCE(SUM(r.amount_minor) OVER (PARTITION BY o.order_id), 0)) / 100.0 * 0.0067

FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id
WHERE o.currency IN ('EUR', 'JPY')

cells.question: Which five apparel products sold the most units?
cells.sql:
SELECT 
    p.product_id,
    p.category,
    SUM(oi.qty) as total_units_sold
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE p.category = 'apparel'
    AND o.status != 'cancelled'
    AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category
ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC
LIMIT 5;

cells.question: What was revenue from apparel products for euro and yen orders, in US dollars?
cells.sql:
SELECT
  SUM(
    COALESCE(order_gross.gross_revenue_usd, 0) - COALESCE(order_refunds.refunds_usd, 0)
  ) AS net_revenue_usd
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    SUM(oi.qty * oi.unit_price_minor) * CASE o.currency
      WHEN 'EUR' THEN 0.0108
      WHEN 'JPY' THEN 0.0067
      WHEN 'USD' THEN 0.01
    END AS gross_revenue_usd
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND o.status != 'cancelled'
    AND c.is_internal = FALSE
    AND p.category = 'apparel'
    AND o.currency IN ('EUR', 'JPY')
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.currency
) order_gross
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    r.order_id,
    SUM(r.amount_minor) * CASE o.currency
      WHEN 'EUR' THEN 0.0108
      WHEN 'JPY' THEN 0.0067
      WHEN 'USD' THEN 0.01
    END AS refunds_usd
  FROM refunds r
  INNER JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND o.status != 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY r.order_id, o.currency
) order_refunds ON order_gross.order_id = order_refunds.order_id;

cells.question: What share of apparel orders ended up with a refund?

  SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id
  FROM orders o

paired.verdict: worker@L0 is worse than worker@L3; we cannot put a number on how much (21 discordant of 36 pairs, McNemar exact p=0.000, clustered)
paired.caveat: McNemar assumes the pairs are independent. These are not: 50 items are 10 clusters of 5 parameterisations, so a systematic weakness in one pattern can produce up to five discordant pairs that are really one observation. The p-value is therefore optimistic and the honest statement is directional only — 'this arm is worse', never a specific gap.
